title: The Hole In A Padlock Lets Water Out, Not In
hook: A hole in a lock, which sounds like a flaw and is a defence.

cast.note: Bill inspects the lock like a suspicious customer, then concedes.

scenes.note: The objection is the hook. Let the viewer think it is a design flaw for a beat.

beats.action: Bill turns a padlock over in his hand
the small hole in the base circles teal
a WATER GETS IN? label lands with an arrow pointing inward
Bill tilts the padlock toward the light to see into the hole
beats.sync: secondary action — closes a pacing gap

scenes.note: Flip the arrow. One beat, one reversal.

beats.action: the inward arrow spins around to point outward; the label crosses out

scenes.note: Water arrives from several directions — the point is that you cannot prevent it.

beats.action: the padlock hangs on a gate in cross-section
droplets arrive from rain, from a hose, from damp air
the droplets collect in the lock body and pool at the bottom
more droplets gather and run down the inside of the body
beats.sync: secondary action — closes a pacing gap

scenes.note: The failure this prevents. Springs and pins seizing — mechanical, not dramatic.

beats.action: a sealed lock body fills with standing water
the pin stack and springs draw inside, submerged
the pins corrode and fuse into one solid mass; the key will not turn
the water crystallises to ice; the shackle locks solid

scenes.note: The fix, and it should feel like relief after the previous scene.

beats.action: the hole opens; the pooled water drains straight out and the pins stay clean

scenes.note: Second use, quick. End on Bill hanging the lock back up.

beats.action: a drop of lubricant enters through the same hole and spreads through the mechanism
Bill snaps the padlock shut and hangs it back on the gate; hard cut
the oil spreads along the pin stack and the shackle frees
beats.sync: secondary action — closes a pacing gap
